studies.citation: Kaiser, J., & Green, C. (2026). Artificial intelligence in the networked public sphere: An analysis of the AI discourse on Twitter. First Monday, 31(4).

methods: remove AI and ArtificialIntelligence from hashtag network
original.data_access: No original dataset or analysis code link found in full article; not a verified original-data replication route.
original.license: Author copyright stated; no dataset/code license found.

adaptation.unit: unique retained post_id within a prespecified bounded search corpus
steps: Use package search with frozen UTC dates, query, language, page/request/time caps and save manifest.
Deduplicate by post ID; report missing language/date/hashtag/URL values instead of imputing.
Produce separate counts by main post, reply, quote and repost; show primary analysis excluding native reposts and an explicitly separate all-retained-posts sensitivity analysis.
Count case-sensitive hashtag post incidence for comparison with Table 2; also export casefolded incidence as an adaptation.
For each post, deduplicate casefolded hashtag strings, exclude ai and artificialintelligence, sort remaining unique tags, increment each unordered distinct pair once.

Use structured expanded URLs already retained by package; urlsplit hostname, lowercase, retain host-level output and document any www normalization; do not guess t.co destination or conflate hostname with registrable domain.
Rank tag and domain incidence; export weighted hashtag edges, nodes, counts and denominator metadata.
Report page-limit/rate-limit/date-filter coverage and observed scope. No total-population shares or claims of exhaustive 2026 AI discourse.
out_of_scope: Gephi community equivalence without full parameters
retweet network when actual retweet edges are absent

adaptation.scope: interaction structure description only; full paper not replicated
steps: Use primary author/institution sites only to build candidate researcher list, then retrieve current profiles through pyXcom.
Apply and log case-insensitive whole-word scientist|researcher|professor to current bio; save matched term and profile observation time. This word-boundary convention is an explicit adaptation.
Retain eligible candidate authors and collect their AI-tool-related root posts in fixed date windows. Purposive seed accounts differ from the original keyword-derived author frame.
Save root candidates before engagement selection; select with a published deterministic rule, preferably chronological/seeded sample, and retain exclusion reasons.
Collect bounded replies through package; keep verified parent/root/depth, unresolved ancestry and retrieval caps.
Separate root-author self-replies from other-author replies. Use other-author replies, not layperson, unless occupational status is independently coded.
Compute retained roots, unique authors, direct vs deeper replies, self-reply share, root-level reply distributions and unresolved-ancestry rate with denominators.
Eligibility for manual-coding sample is at least 3 actually retained resolved replies; displayed platform reply count is not evidence that 3 replies were collected.
Export blank role_code/coder_id/evidence/reference fields. Do not infer roles or run role regressions until validated human annotations exist.
out_of_scope: claim that all reply authors are non-experts
claim that selected famous researchers represent all experts
